data_objects.name: mass_spectra
data_objects.meaning: Mass-spectrum records stored one per TSV row, with a unique record identifier, paired ragged fragment m/z and intensity lists, and precursor metadata.

data_objects.name: molecule_metadata
data_objects.meaning: Molecular structure, identifier, formula, and parent-mass fields embedded in each spectrum row and repeated when multiple spectra refer to the same molecular key.

variables.name: identifier
variables.meaning: Unique spectrum-row identifier formatted as 'MassSpecGymID' followed by digits; no duplicate values occur among the 231,104 records.

variables.name: mzs
variables.meaning: Comma-separated numeric fragment-peak mass-to-charge values forming a variable-length list; positions align with the corresponding intensities list.

variables.name: intensities
variables.meaning: Comma-separated numeric peak-intensity values forming a variable-length list positionally paired with mzs. Dispersed sampled spectra contain positive fractional values with a maximum of 1, but the scaling method is not stated.

variables.name: precursor_formula
variables.meaning: Elemental formula recorded for the precursor species.

variables.name: precursor_mz
variables.meaning: Mass-to-charge value recorded for the precursor ion.

variables.name: adduct
variables.meaning: Bracketed precursor adduct and charge notation; the file contains [M+H]+ and [M+Na]+ values.

variables.name: smiles
variables.meaning: SMILES molecular-structure representation; stereochemical markers are present in some observed strings.

variables.name: inchikey
variables.meaning: Fourteen-character uppercase molecular key used to group repeated molecular records across spectrum rows.

variables.name: formula
variables.meaning: Elemental molecular formula associated with the SMILES record.

variables.name: parent_mass
variables.meaning: Numeric mass value labeled for the parent molecule; the mass convention and physical unit are not documented in the public file.

structure.description: massspecgym.tsv is a denormalized 10-column table with 231,104 data rows. Each row is one spectrum record keyed by identifier. mzs and intensities are comma-delimited ragged arrays whose element counts match in every row; their shared position defines each peak, and representative lists are ordered by increasing m/z. Molecule fields are repeated at spectrum granularity: the same inchikey can occur in multiple rows with distinct identifiers and peak lists, establishing a one-to-many molecule-to-spectrum relationship in the table.

uncertainties: The public file does not state the instrument, acquisition method, ionization source, collision conditions, retention information, or whether the spectra are raw or processed.
The intensity unit and scaling or normalization procedure are undocumented; sampled values peaking at 1 do not establish a specific normalization rule.

The physical unit and mass definition for parent_mass are not stated. For mzs and precursor_mz, the field names establish mass-to-charge semantics but no separate unit convention or calibration metadata is supplied.

Every inchikey value is 14 characters rather than a complete multi-block InChIKey. The values appear to be connectivity-block keys, but the public file does not document the truncation or its intended identity scope.

No tab-separated field is blank, but the file provides no explicit missing-value or sentinel-value declaration; no alternative sentinel was identified in the bounded representative content inspection.
The meaning of the numeric suffix and any semantic significance of physical row ordering are not documented.
annotation_notes: Evidence was restricted to the single public artifact massspecgym.tsv and the routed mass-spectrometry inspection reference.

The public artifact is a 257,027,435-byte ASCII TSV with one header row and 231,104 data rows. A structural pass found exactly 10 fields in every row, no blank fields, no duplicate identifier values, and no mzs/intensities length mismatches.

Representative records from the beginning, quarter points, midpoint, and end were used to inspect peak ordering, numeric encodings, molecular representations, and precursor fields; no task, answer, private artifact, or external source was used.
